name: Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum
alias_note: The tester added the venue on the phone as 'Cooper Hewitt' with slug 'cooper-hewitt' (take 2026-09-29, a low-confidence venue_added record). The registry slug is the same, so the two join without a mapping. The full name is from the venue sign (f0001): 'COOPER HEWITT / Smithsonian Design Museum'.

location.address_note: Not on any frame from the visit. Fill from the institution's own page, not from memory (§8.2).
location.footprint_note: From the take's own fixes (2026-09-29): the three venue-sign frames at the entrance fall within 40.78453–40.78466 N, 73.95760–73.95797 W. Every frame after the first label carries one fix from 20:16:20 UTC, including the exterior shot 17 minutes later — the phone produced no new fix indoors — so the interior has no GPS evidence of its own. A single point with a ~150 m radius covers the building.

collection_api.notes: Cooper Hewitt's own collection site (collection.cooperhewitt.org) now redirects to si.edu behind a request-verification page, which answers scripts with 403; it is not to be worked around. Two machine-readable primary sources remain, both the museum's own data (constraint 6 does not apply). (1) The Smithsonian Open Access API, unit_code CHNDM: a free api.data.gov key (keychain item 'placard-si-api'); the shared DEMO_KEY is exhausted within a dozen calls. It holds only the CC0 subset, 58,198 Cooper Hewitt records on 2026-09-29, and none of the nine objects from the first visit are in it: modern design is mostly in copyright. A record is fetched as /content/edanmdm:chndm_<accession>, and full-text search tokenizes on the hyphens, so searching a number returns noise. (2) The museum's published dataset, github.com/cooperhewitt/collection, CC0: meta/objects.csv (194,316 objects, accession_number, title, date, medium, creditline, year_acquired, url) and meta/objects-participants.csv (designers, makers, donors, with nationality and dates). Last pushed 2018-01-10, so it covers objects acquired through 2017 and records as they stood then; 2018-40-1 and 2025-11-1 are not in it. Fixtures verified this way say verified_against 'catalog_dataset'.

accession_formats.policy: LOCATE, DO NOT VALIDATE (D11, D21). Patterns rank candidates; nothing is rejected for failing them.
accession_formats.catalog_census: Measured over the museum's published objects.csv (194,316 objects, 2026-09-29): 192,248 (98.9%) begin YYYY-N-N, and in every one of them the first component equals the record's year_acquired. 127,858 are exactly three groups, 41,044 four; about 21,000 carry a lower-case part designator (-c, -a,b, -a/g).

shapes.notes: Year of acquisition, then the lot within that year, then the item within the lot. Dominant shape: 66% of the catalog.
A fourth group numbers the leaves of a portfolio or album (1921-6-548-138). 21% of the catalog; not yet seen on a label.

accession_formats.part_designators: A hyphen and lower-case letters after the number — '-a,b' (a kettle and its lid), '-a/d' (a range), '-c'. The locator keeps them on the token and strips them before matching a shape, as it does MCNY's '14A-B' (D24).
accession_formats.locating_heuristic: Last on the credit line, after a comma, with no parentheses: 'Gift of Donald M. Genaro, 2018-40-1'. The line often wraps so the number sits alone on the next line. The credit line carries no separate year: the key's first component IS the acquisition year, so the locator's credit-year agreement fires on the key itself. That is harmless here, and true.
traps: THE NUMBERS LOOK LIKE DATES. On the first visit the tester answered 'no number' on four of eight labels because '2018-40-1' read as a date — and the phone had offered the right number every time. Validity as a calendar date does not separate them: 154,082 catalog numbers have a middle group above 12, but 13,021 (6.8%) are real calendar dates (2015-1-18, 2025-11-1). The read-back is where this has to be solved, not the locator.

Old-style figures in the credit line's serif — descending 3, 4, 5, 7, 9 and a small-cap-like 1 — sit beside lining figures in the title's sans. Vision read both correctly on every label of the first visit.

Shorthand lists: 'Gift of Gerald Gulotta, 2009-16-6, 7-a, 8-a,b, 11' is four objects — 2009-16-6, 2009-16-7-a (catalog: 2009-16-7-a/d), 2009-16-8-a,b and 2009-16-11. Only the first is a complete token; the rest inherit its prefix.

One credit line can cover two numbers with different credits: 'Museum purchase through bequest of Ida McNeil…, 1992-131-8, 1992-132-1-a,b' — the catalog credits the drawing 1992-131-8 as a gift of the designer. The first number on a line is not necessarily the photographed object.

Shared panels keyed by black silhouettes, one per object, instead of numbers or positions (the 'Vessel / Sculptura telephone / Vase' panel). The silhouette is the only thing that ties a tombstone to an object in the case.

dialects.format: printed on brushed metal, in a perforated channel, a vitrine edge or a free-standing panel
dialects.typeface: bold sans (title, date) over a serif with old-style figures (everything else)
field_order: title, date — 'Paper dress, 1966'; the object name is part of the title, with the proper name italic
maker line(s): 'Designed by …', 'Manufactured by …', 'Made by …', each person with (nationality, dates) and each firm with (city, region, country)
credit line, small type, ending with the accession
interpretive paragraph, often on a separate plate below
dialects.has_silhouette_key: Most cards carry a black silhouette of the object at the left or top — a pictogram, not text. Shared panels use it to tell objects apart.

labels.photography_note: The field log says 'unknown'; no photography sign was photographed.
labels.lighting: Dim, warm, with glass vitrines throughout; the tester tagged reflective_glass on seven of nine groups.

access_rules.reservation_note: The same sign says 'Reserve your tickets online at cooperhewitt.org' without saying whether that applies to the pay-what-you-wish hour.

access_rules_note: Pay what you wish is not free, so it is its own kind rather than a free_window. The field log records the visit as 'Paid'.

accessibility.note: A 'PRESS TO OPERATE DOOR' button with the wheelchair symbol, beside curved stone steps (f0003). Whether that door is step-free is not visible in the frame; the main door in the exterior shot (f0028) is up several steps.
